items.content_html:
Summary

Add some keys representing a new behavior in module loading, where HTTP errors aren't cached, so developers can now retry loading a module that failed to fetch.

Test results and supporting details

This is a spec change and (I think) one that is impossible to feature detect, so this makes a good fit for a behavioral subfeature.

I didn't test this, but it's well attested through bugs:

  • Chromium enabled it in 156 (tracking bug).
  • WebKit added it with r319474. The Safari TP release notes don't mention it by name, but it was included in the range of changes given by the 252 release notes. When I tried the WPT test on Safari 27, it failed.
  • Firefox bug 2055211 shows this shipping in 154.

Setting the spec URL was difficult. There's nothing in the spec that screams that this should work the way it does, but you can see whatwg/html#10327 and tell me if you've got a better idea here.

Lastly, I added three keys since I believe these are the three entry points for this behavior. See #30304 for further discussion.

Related issues

  • Fixes #30304
  • Prompted by web-platform-dx/web-features#4335
  • Spec change: whatwg/html#10327
items.title: Add retriable module loading keys

items.content_html:
Summary

The window-drag CSS property is supported in Chrome 152, but only on desktop: see https://chromestatus.com/feature/5201338641285120. This PR therefore sets its support on mobile to false.

Engineering confirmed this, saying: "it isn't supported on Android, but WebView has a sister CoreWebView2WindowControlsOverlay which supports draggable regions. I would update Android to false."

But that sounds like support for an equivalent feature on WebView, so I think WebView should still be false.

Test results and supporting details

Related issues
items.title: window-drag not supported on mobile

Summary

Test results and supporting details

Found using the OWD Collector project (v10.20.11, but a local development branch with support for collecting flags).

Chromestatus: https://chromestatus.com/feature/5137581018841088
Behind a flag since v146: https://chromiumdash.appspot.com/commit/832e11ef197bd8a4b8c9a778e49480d1f994be20
The constructor is not implemented: https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/main:third_party/blink/renderer/core/html/forms/autofill_event.idl?q=AutofillEvent%20idl

Related issues

None.
